column1: Azure SQL Database is a fully managed {{c1::platform-as-a-service (PaaS)}} database offering.
column2:
Microsoft manages the underlying infrastructure and engine maintenance.
Review source

column1: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines uses the {{c1::infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS)}} deployment model.
column2:
You retain control over the operating system and SQL Server instance.
Review source

column1: The documented maximum storage size for a single Azure SQL Database Hyperscale database is {{c1::128 TB}}.
column2:
Storage grows automatically up to a service limit, not without a limit.
Review source

column1: In Azure SQL Managed Instance, In-Memory OLTP requires the {{c1::Business Critical}} service tier.
column2:
The feature supports memory-optimized transactional objects.
Review source

column1: Azure SQL Managed Instance supports reliable asynchronous database messaging through {{c1::Service Broker}}.
column2:
This is an instance-level capability available in Managed Instance.
Review source

column1: Azure SQL Managed Instance sends email through {{c1::Database Mail}} using an external SMTP server.
column2:
SMTP means Simple Mail Transfer Protocol.
Review source

column1: Azure SQL Managed Instance supports {{c1::linked servers}} for accessing configured remote data sources.
column2:
Supported providers and remote configurations still have platform-specific limits.
Review source

column1: For SQL Server on Azure VMs, {{c1::Always On availability groups}} provide a database-replica-based high-availability option.
column2:
You configure the replicas and failover design.
Review source

column1: For a SQL Server Azure VM, {{c1::SQL best practices assessment}} checks configuration against recommended settings.
column2:
This feature is available through the SQL IaaS Agent extension.
Review source

column1: SQL database in Fabric mirrors data into OneLake as {{c1::Delta Parquet files}}.
column2:
Analytics queries can read these copies instead of querying the operational tables directly.
Review source

column1: SQL database in Fabric replicates operational changes to OneLake in {{c1::near real time}}.
column2:
Replication lag means the analytical copy can trail the source.
Review source

column1: From a Fabric SQL analytics endpoint, cross-item table references use {{c1::three-part names}} such as WarehouseName.dbo.TableName.
column2:
This capability belongs to the analytical endpoint, not arbitrary cross-database access from the transactional engine.
Review source

column1: Fabric source control provides {{c1::Git}} integration for SQL database development.
column2:
Version control tracks database changes separately from running application transactions.
Review source

column1: The Fabric portal can expose a SQL database through a {{c1::GraphQL API}}.
column2:
This provides an API interface over database data.
Review source
